input_format: raw sequence of HTTP/2 wire DATA frames
configuration_profile: real DATA handlers with preread, no-buffering request-body, bounded body-filter, multi-frame body, Content-Length validation, and single-/multi-frame padded-body profiles including mixed and long alternating padding sequences
allocator_mode: NGX_DEBUG_PALLOC=1 with a fresh nginx pool for each fragmentation replay
justification: NGX-IF12/13 cover connection control and stream reset, but not DATA padding, preread payload accumulation and receive-window state.
state: Each input is parsed eight times across four fragmentation schedules in preread and no-buffering profiles. Structurally valid unpadded single DATA frames on stream 1 are parsed through bounded body-filter profiles with chunked, matching Content-Length, and too-short Content-Length settings; the overrun result is captured before synthetic request finalization. END_STREAM frames also run a profile declaring one byte more than the body, simulating the body-read flush continuation and requiring ngx_http_v2_filter_request_body to return NGX_HTTP_BAD_REQUEST for the underrun. Structurally valid padded single DATA frames with more than 16 body bytes after padding are run through the real body filter with an exact Content-Length under four network-fragment schedules. Valid multi-frame DATA sequences are additionally run through a persistent request_body buffer and filter chain, ending with END_STREAM. Sequences where every DATA frame is validly padded and total unpadded body exceeds 16 bytes are parsed through the same shared request_body buffer and filter chain under four network-fragment schedules. Mixed-padding sequences with at least one padded and one unpadded DATA frame, valid final END_STREAM, and more than 16 unpadded body bytes use the same shared path and fragmentation schedules. A dedicated long-sequence profile requires at least six valid DATA frames, five padding-state transitions, and at least 48 unpadded body bytes; it reuses the shared request_body buffer and filter chain under the four fragmentation schedules.
known_limitations: Only DATA frames are accepted and only stream ID 1 has a synthetic live request.

The request_body profiles exercise ngx_http_v2_process_request_body; gated body-filter profiles isolate structurally valid DATA and multi-frame sequences and exercise ngx_http_v2_filter_request_body with a consuming no-op sink. A fuzz-only guard captures body validation errors before synthetic request finalization. The underrun profile explicitly simulates the body-read flush continuation after END_STREAM. Matching-length and single-frame padded-body profiles simulate the body-read flush continuation; padded multi-frame inputs retain one shared request_body state across all frames. Downstream body filters, application processing and a full HEADERS-to-request path are not entered.
Inputs are capped at 4096 bytes, so large-frame receive-window exhaustion is not reachable.

scopes.contract: Validate DATA stream identifier, padding and receive windows; skip unknown or closed streams; consume payload through preread, request_body and bounded filter-chain paths; preserve request-body state across multiple DATA frames and honor final END_STREAM.
scopes.preconditions: Fresh HTTP/2 connection with one active stream ID 1, a valid core location conf, an 8192-byte preread buffer or a 16-byte request_body buffer, and a consuming no-op top body filter.
variants: full body buffer and chain flush
body shorter than Content-Length at END_STREAM
padded multi-frame body through shared filter buffer
mixed padded and unpadded multi-frame body through shared filter buffer
mixed padding with varied DATA frame payload lengths
six-frame alternating padding with repeated shared-buffer flushes
padded DATA after 15 accumulated body bytes
padded DATA after 16 accumulated body bytes
padded DATA after 17 accumulated body bytes
padding lengths 0, 1 and 255 at each 15/16/17-byte body boundary
